security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate frontend artifact builder, but it runs shell scripts with package installation and file-system side effects. Most markdown, URL, and local configuration findings are false positives; the remaining concerns are supply-chain exposure, global package installation, and a packaged component archive that reduces reviewability.

remediation.issue: Runtime dependency installation from public package registries
remediation.suggestion: Pin exact package versions, avoid latest package creation commands, and ask for user confirmation before installing dependencies.

remediation.issue: Global pnpm installation when pnpm is missing
remediation.suggestion: Avoid npm install -g in the skill script or require users to install pnpm themselves before running setup.

remediation.issue: Bundled component archive is extracted into source code
remediation.suggestion: Store component files as normal text files or verify the archive checksum and reject absolute or parent-directory paths before extraction.

remediation.issue: Shell scripts perform project writes and build cleanup
remediation.suggestion: Document every side effect and keep deletion limited to generated build outputs inside the current project directory.

semantic_findings.title: Runtime Package Installation from Public Registries
semantic_findings.description: The initializer and bundler install packages during execution, including global pnpm installation when missing and frontend dependencies from npm or pnpm registries. This creates supply-chain and environment modification risk even though it appears related to the skill purpose.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The package installation commands are explicit and occur automatically as part of normal setup and bundling. The risk is supply-chain exposure, not evidence of malicious intent.

semantic_findings.title: Packaged Component Archive Extracted into Source
semantic_findings.description: The setup script extracts shadcn-components.tar.gz into the generated src directory. The archive listing contains expected relative component paths, but the archive format can hide source contents from normal text review and lacks checksum validation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The extraction command and bundled archive are present, and the archive is part of the published skill. Manual listing reduced concern about path traversal, but the package remains less reviewable than plain source files.

content.value_statement: Complex HTML artifacts need project structure, reusable components, and reliable bundling. This skill creates a React workspace and packages it into one HTML artifact for Claude conversations.
actual_capabilities: Creates a React 18 and TypeScript project with Vite.
Configures Tailwind CSS with shadcn/ui theme variables.
Adds path aliases for imports from the src directory.
Installs Radix UI and common shadcn/ui dependencies.
Extracts a prepared set of shadcn/ui component files.
Bundles the app into one inlined HTML file with Parcel.
limitations: Requires Node.js 18 or newer and pnpm-compatible package installation.
Runs shell scripts that install dependencies and modify project files.
Best suited for complex artifacts, not simple single-file snippets.
The bundled component archive should be reviewed before production use.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui project for building complex HTML artifacts.

faq.question: Can it make a single shareable file?
faq.answer: Yes. The bundling script creates one HTML file with scripts, styles, and assets inlined.

faq.question: Does it need package installation?
faq.answer: Yes. The scripts install frontend dependencies with pnpm and may install pnpm globally if it is missing.

faq.question: Is it safe for simple artifacts?
faq.answer: It is usually unnecessary for simple artifacts because it adds project setup and dependency installation.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users review first?
faq.answer: Users should review the shell scripts, dependency installation steps, and bundled shadcn/ui component archive.
